item.title: collabora-online: 24.04.13-2 → 24.04.17-3
item.description:
Update collabora-online to mitigate CVE mentioned in #487562.

This is not the overall latest version (which is 25.04.8-3), but the latest version in the 24.04 branch. (for easier backporting to NixOS 25.11; and also I haven't tested the 25.04 branch)

Also the update script now accepts an optional version argument.

Things done

  • Built on platform:
    • [x] x86_64-linux
    • [ ] aarch64-linux
    • [ ] x86_64-darwin
    • [ ] aarch64-darwin
  • Tested, as applicable:
    • [ ] NixOS tests in nixos/tests.
    • [ ] Package tests at passthru.tests.
    • [ ] Tests in lib/tests or pkgs/test for functions and "core" functionality.
  • [ ] Ran nixpkgs-review on this PR. See nixpkgs-review usage.
  • [x] Tested basic functionality of all binary files, usually in ./result/bin/. (see "How to run" section below)
  • Nixpkgs Release Notes
    • [ ] Package update: when the change is major or breaking.
  • NixOS Release Notes
    • [ ] Module addition: when adding a new NixOS module.
    • [ ] Module update: when the change is significant.
  • [ ] Fits CONTRIBUTING.md, pkgs/README.md, maintainers/README.md and other READMEs.

How to run

It's a slightly modernized version of my instruction from #330708.

How to run

  1. Build VM Grab this definition of NixOS VM and replace myawesomehostname with the hostname of your host. (the VM and the host should have the same hostname)

    vm.nix 
    let
  hostname = "myawesomehostname"; # Replace with your hostname
in
{
  "${hostname}" =
    { config, pkgs, ... }:
    {
      services.nextcloud = {
        enable = true;
        hostName = hostname;
        config.adminpassFile = "/etc/nextcloud-admin-pass";
        config.dbtype = "sqlite";
        extraApps = {
          inherit (config.services.nextcloud.package.packages.apps) richdocuments;
        };
      };
      environment.etc."nextcloud-admin-pass".text = "a";

      services.collabora-online = {
        enable = true;
        settings = {
          ssl.enable = false;
          ssl.termination = false;
        };
        aliasGroups = [ { host = "http://${hostname}"; } ];
      };

      systemd.services.nextcloud-setup-collabora = {
        after = [ "nextcloud-setup.service" ];
        wantedBy = [ "multi-user.target" ];
        path = [ config.services.nextcloud.occ ];
        serviceConfig = {
          Type = "oneshot";
          User = "nextcloud";
          ExecStart = pkgs.writeScript "nextcloud-setup-collabora.sh" ''
            #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
            nextcloud-occ config:app:set richdocuments disable_certificate_verification --value yes
            nextcloud-occ richdocuments:setup --wopi-url=http://${hostname}:9980
          '';
        };
      };

      networking.firewall.enable = false;
      virtualisation = {
        forwardPorts = [
          {
            from = "host";
            guest.port = 80;
            host.port = 80;
          }
          {
            from = "host";
            guest.port = 9980;
            host.port = 9980;
          }
        ];
      };

      system.stateVersion = "26.05";
    };
}

    Build it with the following command:

    NIXPKGS_PATH=/path/to/nixpkgs # Replace this with your path

NIX_PATH=nixpkgs=$NIXPKGS_PATH nix-shell "$NIXPKGS_PATH" -A nixos-build-vms --run 'nixos-build-vms ./vm.nix'

  2. Run VM

    sudo ./result/bin/nixos-run-vms

    Sudo is required to bind the VM to port 80.

  3. Login In a browser, go to http://myawesomehostname. It will prompt you with a login page. Enter root and a.

  4. Create a new document In the top left corner select "Files", then "+ New", then "New Document". Press "Create". Click on the newly created document to open it. The Collabora Online editor should appear.

  5. Verify version In the top menubar select "Help", then "About". In the appeared window:

    • "COOLWSD version" is related to nixpkgs.collabora-online aka the web service.
    • "LOKit version" is related to nixpkgs.libreoffice-collabora aka fork of LibreOffice that this web service uses.

item.title: [25.11] nixos/captive-browser: remove the udhcpc wrapper unless required
item.description:
Remove the udhcpc setcap wrapper unless required as it allows any user to execute arbitrary commands with the cap_net_raw capability. Additionally, if it is required, warn the user and explain how they can avoid the issue.

Mitigates CVE-2026-25740

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/security/advisories/GHSA-wc3r-c66x-8xmc
